- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0), model frequently overcorrects with a steep drop; cap forecast decline to 15–20% of peak.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) for 3+ consecutive days, model shows mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply linear decay to forecast values from day 1–7, reducing by 10–15% per day.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth forecast with weighted average of 3–5 recent values.
